title: From Human Labels to Literature: Semi-Supervised Learning of NMR Chemical Shifts at Scale
abstract: arXiv:2601.18524v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Accurate prediction of nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) chemical shifts is fundamental to spectral analysis and molecular structure elucidation, yet existing machine learning methods rely on limited, labor-intensive atom-assigned datasets. We propose a semi-supervised framework that learns NMR chemical shifts from millions of literature-extracted spectra without explicit atom-level assignments, integrating a small amount of labeled data with large-scale unassigned spectra. We formulate chemical shift prediction from literature spectra as a permutation-invariant set supervision problem, and show that under commonly satisfied conditions on the loss function, optimal bipartite matching reduces to a sorting-based loss, enabling stable large-scale semi-supervised training beyond traditional curated datasets. Our models achieve substantially improved accuracy and robustness over state-of-the-art methods and exhibit stronger generalization

translated_title: 从人工标注到文献：大规模核磁共振化学位移的半监督学习
translated_abstract: 核磁共振（NMR）化学位移的准确预测是谱图分析和分子结构解析的基础，然而现有的机器学习方法依赖于有限的、需要大量人工劳动的原子级标注数据集。我们提出了一种半监督框架，能够从数百万个文献提取的谱图中学习NMR化学位移，而无需显式的原子级标注，将少量标注数据与大规模未标注谱图相结合。我们将从文献谱图中预测化学位移的问题表述为置换不变的集合监督问题，并证明在损失函数满足通常可满足的条件下，最优二分匹配可以简化为基于排序的损失，从而实现超越传统精选数据集的稳定大规模半监督训练。我们的模型在准确性和鲁棒性方面显著优于最先进的方法，并展现出更强的泛化能力。
tldr: 本文提出一种半监督学习框架，利用数百万个无需原子级标注的文献谱图大规模学习核磁共振化学位移预测，显著提升了预测准确性、鲁棒性和泛化能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a semi-supervised learning framework that trains NMR chemical shift predictors at scale using millions of literature-extracted spectra without atom-level assignments, achieving substantially improved accuracy, robustness, and generalization over state-of-the-art methods.
